verbose: Sorry, I think my internet is very slow today, my voice may be breaking in between, so if you are not able to hear me properly then please tell me immediately, I will switch off my video and try.
reference: My connection's a bit iffy, so shout if I break up and I'll kill my video.

verbose: Since I am not able to join the standup meeting today because of a doctor appointment, I am writing my update here only, yesterday I finished the report and today I will start working on the presentation.
reference: Can't make stand-up — doctor's appointment. Report's done; starting the deck today.

verbose: As per the new policy, all employees have to come to the office minimum three days in a week, and the team managers will decide which three days, so please coordinate with your manager regarding the same.
reference: The policy's three office days a week, set by managers, so do liaise with yours.

verbose: Working from home full-time is good for saving the travel time, but honestly I am feeling very lonely sometimes, because I don't talk to anybody the whole day except in the work meetings.
reference: Home working saves the commute, but I miss a natter outside meetings.

verbose: People are sending me messages at eleven o'clock in the night and expecting an immediate reply from me, which is not fair at all, because I also need some personal time after the working hours are over.
reference: Once I've clocked off, I shouldn't be expected to reply at eleven at night.

verbose: Since we started working from home, the number of meetings has increased so much, every small thing is becoming a meeting, which could have been done by just sending one simple message on chat.
reference: Since going remote, our meeting discipline's gone to pot — half could be a message.

verbose: Before I log off for the day, I am sharing the status of the deployment with the team in the other time zone, so they can continue the work from where I am leaving it, and nothing gets stuck overnight.
reference: Before logging off, I'll post a handover so nothing stalls overnight.

verbose: Onboarding a new joiner remotely is very difficult, because they cannot just turn around and ask the person sitting next to them, so we should give them one buddy whom they can message anytime they want.
reference: Remote onboarding is hard, so let's give each new starter a buddy to message.

verbose: Can we please shift tomorrow's meeting to little bit later, maybe after twelve o'clock, because I am having to drop my child at school in the morning and I will not be able to join on time.
reference: Could we move tomorrow's meeting to after twelve? I've got the school run.

verbose: I think instead of expecting everyone to reply immediately on chat, we should accept that people may reply after some time, because everyone is working in different hours and they need some time to focus.
reference: With everyone on flexitime, let's not expect instant replies on chat.

verbose: The company has said that they will give some money to everybody for buying a good chair and desk for working from home, so you can buy them and submit the bills to the finance team for reimbursement.
reference: The company's chipping in for a decent chair and desk — send receipts to finance.

verbose: I think there is some misunderstanding because of the message I sent yesterday, I didn't mean it in a rude way at all, it's just that I was typing very quickly and it came out wrong, so please don't feel bad about it.
reference: It's easy to get the wrong end of the stick on chat. I was rushed, not rude.
targets: get the wrong end of the stick

verbose: For every meeting, please share the agenda one day before only, so that everybody can come prepared and we don't waste the first ten minutes understanding what the meeting is about.
reference: Please share an agenda the day before, so we don't waste ten minutes.

verbose: Since everybody is coming to the office on Wednesday, I am thinking we should use that day for the team discussions and brainstorming, and do the individual focus work on the home days instead.
reference: Let's allocate Wednesdays, when we're all in, to team discussions.

verbose: When you are working from home, sometimes the managers don't know how much work you are doing actually, so it is important to share your updates regularly so that your work is visible to them.
reference: Working remotely, effort can go unnoticed, so don't be shy to blow your own trumpet.

verbose: Sorry for the background noise, there is some construction work going on in the building next to my house, and it is very loud, I will keep myself on mute when I am not talking, okay.
reference: Sorry about the racket — building work next door. I'll stay on mute.

verbose: One thing that is not working well is that the people who are in the office are having discussions among themselves and taking decisions, and the people at home are not getting to know about it.
reference: Office staff decide things among themselves and remote people find out later. It's not joined-up.

verbose: Just informing you all that tomorrow I will be on half day leave because I have to go to the bank and some other personal work also, so I will be available only till one o'clock.
reference: I'm off from one tomorrow, so catch me in the morning.

verbose: We are using too many different tools for communication, some people are on email, some on chat, some on the other app, and important messages are getting lost in between all this.
reference: Our comms are at sixes and sevens across three tools, so messages get lost.

verbose: Since we are all working remotely, we are not knowing each other personally at all, so I am suggesting we should do one online game or quiz every Friday for thirty minutes, just for fun.
reference: A Friday quiz would help break the ice — we barely know each other.

verbose: Sorry to cut you in between, but I think we are going out of the topic, the meeting was for discussing the budget, and we are talking about the office party from last fifteen minutes.
reference: Sorry to interrupt, but we've drifted — this was meant to be about the budget.

verbose: Some managers are feeling that people are not working properly from home, but actually the data is clearly showing that the productivity has increased after we started working from home.
reference: The data doesn't corroborate those doubts — productivity's risen since we went remote.

verbose: Coming to the office takes me almost two hours in one direction because of the traffic, so four hours daily are going waste in travelling only, that is why I prefer working from home.
reference: With two-hour tailbacks each way, working from home makes more sense.

verbose: Please check my calendar once before booking any meeting with me, because many times people are booking meetings during my lunch time or when I am already in another meeting, and then I am having to reschedule everything again and again.
reference: I'd be grateful if you'd check my calendar before booking — I keep getting double-booked.

verbose: We are planning one team offsite next month where the whole team will meet in person for two days, there will be some planning sessions in the day and also some fun activities in the evening.
reference: Next month's away day: two days in person, planning by day, fun by night.

verbose: When some people are in the meeting room and some people are joining online, the people online are not able to hear properly what is being said in the room, so we need a better microphone.
reference: Remote attendees can't hear the room, so they end up playing second fiddle.

verbose: I wanted to ask if I can work from my hometown for two weeks next month, because my parents are not keeping well, and I will be available during all the working hours as usual, no change.
reference: Do you mind if I work from my parents' for a fortnight? They're poorly.

verbose: When you are writing the messages on chat, please write the full information in one message only, instead of writing hi, and then waiting for reply, and then writing the actual question, which is wasting everybody's time unnecessarily.
reference: On chat, cut to the chase — ask your question in one go, not just "hi".

verbose: I will be travelling tomorrow for the whole day, so I will not be able to join any calls at all, but I will be checking my messages in between whenever possible, so you can message me if urgent.
reference: I'm travelling tomorrow, so no calls, but I'll pop online when I can.

verbose: Since working from home, I am noticing that I am working more hours than before, because there is no clear end of the day, and I keep on checking the emails even late in the evening.
reference: Since going remote, I find it hard to wind down — I check email all evening.

verbose: Coming to the office five days a week again will be very difficult for many people, especially those who are having small children, and some people may even leave the company because of this.
reference: A five-day return would be detrimental to parents especially, and we might lose people.

verbose: Since we are working remotely, everything should be written down properly in the shared documents, because people cannot just walk to your desk and ask, and the verbal discussions are getting forgotten.
reference: Remotely, we need decisions and minutes written down, as verbal agreements get forgotten.

verbose: After back-to-back video calls the whole day, I am feeling very tired by the evening, my eyes are paining, and I am not able to concentrate on any actual work after that.
reference: Back-to-back video calls leave me worn out, with sore eyes and no focus.

verbose: I am proposing that we should all agree on some rules for the team, like reply to messages within four hours, keep the status updated, and inform others if you are going away from the desk.
reference: Rule of thumb: reply within four hours, keep your status current, flag when you step away.

verbose: We did the interview on video call, and the candidate was very good, but I feel we should meet once in person also before finalising, because it is a senior role and the person will be leading a whole team.
reference: She tops our shortlist, but for a senior role I'd want to meet in person first.

verbose: Sorry everyone, my internet got disconnected suddenly in between, and I missed the last five minutes of the discussion, can somebody please tell me quickly what was decided just now.
reference: Sorry, I dropped off for five minutes. Could someone help me catch up?

verbose: Some days I am going to the coworking space near my house instead of working from home, because at home there are too many distractions, and at least there I can focus properly on my work.
reference: At home I end up pottering about, so some days I use a co-working space.

verbose: Since we are not meeting in the office, I want to have one short call with each of you every week, just to check how you are doing, not only about the work but in general also.
reference: Let's touch base weekly, one to one — not just work, but how you're doing.

verbose: When you are working from a café or any public place, please make sure nobody is able to see your screen, and do not connect to the free public WiFi without using the VPN, it is very risky.
reference: Use discretion with your screen in public, and never use open Wi-Fi without the VPN.

verbose: From this month onwards, everybody has to fill the timesheet every Friday, mentioning how many hours they have worked on each project, because the finance team needs it for billing the clients.
reference: From this month, please fill in your timesheet every Friday for client billing.

verbose: In the hybrid meetings, the people in the room are talking among themselves and forgetting about the people online, so the chairperson should make sure everyone online also gets a chance to speak in the discussion.
reference: Online attendees can't get a word in edgeways, so the chair must bring them in.

verbose: Sorry I am joining late, actually the previous meeting got extended by fifteen minutes and I could not leave in between because my manager was presenting something very important.
reference: Apologies — my last meeting dragged on.

verbose: Please don't schedule the meetings at six in the morning for the team in the other country, it is not fair to them at all, we should find a time which is reasonable for both the sides.
reference: Six a.m. calls aren't equitable — let's find a time that suits both offices.

verbose: I am blocking two hours every morning in my calendar for focused work, so during that time I will not be joining any meetings or replying to messages, except if it is something very urgent.
reference: I'm ring-fencing two hours each morning for focus — urgent things only.

verbose: I just want to give a big thanks to the support team, they handled all the customer issues during the outage so well, even though most of them were working from home with no proper setup.
reference: Huge thanks to support for going the extra mile during the outage, mostly from home.

verbose: Please don't use the main team channel for personal discussions and jokes, because important announcements are getting lost in between all these messages, you can create one separate channel for that.
reference: Please keep the main channel for work. Banter can go elsewhere.

verbose: For the people who could not join the meeting because of the time difference, I have recorded the full session and put it in the shared folder, so they can watch it whenever they are free.
reference: The recording's in the shared folder for other time zones — help yourself.

verbose: Today was my first day back in the office after one full year, and honestly it was very nice to meet everybody in person, though the travelling was little bit tiring for me, and I was feeling sleepy also.
reference: First day back in a year — lovely to see everyone, though the commute was tiring.

verbose: After every meeting, nobody is knowing who is supposed to do what, because we discuss many things but we are not writing down who is responsible for each action point in the minutes.
reference: Let's give every action an owner — we leave meetings unsure who's doing what.

verbose: I am apologising in advance because my kids are at home today due to the school holiday, so there may be some disturbance in the background, but I will try my best to manage it.
reference: The kids are home for half-term, so bear with me if it's noisy.

verbose: I wanted to share that the new hybrid working arrangement is going quite well so far, people are liking the flexibility, but some teams are still facing difficulty in planning the office days, and they are fighting with each other about which day to come in.
reference: Hybrid's going well — people love the flexibility, though some teams are still ironing out office days.

verbose: I am not very comfortable giving negative feedback to my team members on a video call, because I cannot read their reaction properly, and sometimes they are taking it in the wrong way.
reference: Tricky feedback over video is hard — you lose the nuance.

verbose: Since we are hiring fully remote, we can get good people from any part of the country, not only from the city where our office is, which gives us a much bigger talent pool to choose from.
reference: Hiring remotely lets us leverage talent from anywhere, not just near the office.

verbose: I think we have discussed everything which was there in the agenda, so if nobody is having any other points to discuss, we can finish the meeting now and everyone can get back to their work.
reference: That's the agenda covered. Any other business? If not, let's wrap up.

verbose: I will not be available on Thursday afternoon because of a family function, so if any client calls are coming during that time, can you please handle them on my behalf, if possible and let me know what happened.
reference: Could you fill in for me on client calls Thursday afternoon? I'm at a family do.
